card.name: Plural subjects after quantifiers like some or many
card.fires_on: The word or word end right after a quantifier or generalizing phrase such as 'some', 'many' or 'frequently', where a plural group noun or verb is expected. It marks a general claim about a group, in ordinary web prose.

modes.label: Group noun after some/many
modes.description: A plural noun that completes a phrase like 'in some' or 'many traditional'.
modes.example: in many traditional<< societies>> there are few other available money-earning

modes.label: Verb or relative word after a plural subject
modes.description: A verb or 'who' following a plural subject, often with a frequency adverb.
modes.example: Gardeners frequently<< state>> that they would adopt environmentally preferable lawn care

card.plain: It lights up when a sentence is making a general statement about some or many people or things, right after the group is named.
